messages:
anya: Heads-up: during the pin/unpin refactor I started seeing transient leaked pins when tenants rapidly export/import pages between processes. repro is flaky but reproducible under high interleaving.

sam: can you share a tiny trace? sounds like ordering between detach and free again.

anya: short trace: export(fd) -> importer mmap -> allocator_free on host-pinned path -> exporter close(fd) -> later dma_buf_detach happens but pages still show live pins. sometimes the importer never does the final release syscall because it took a fastpath shortcut.

jorge: last time our fix was to rely on refcounts but that feels brittle with async worker reordering. we should consider an explicit transfer token rather than implicit refcounts for imported pages.

maria: agree. explicit token can encode the allocator generation + a small nonce. the importer holds the token until it's ready to give up pins, then calls allocator_handoff_done(token). until then allocator treats the pages as HANDOFF_PENDING and won't reuse them.

sam: token approach OK, but we must avoid blocking free on hot paths. propose a nonblocking state machine: ACTIVE -> PENDING_HANDOFF (token issued) -> RELEASED. allocator_free sets PENDING_HANDOFF and continues, but marks the page as non-reusable. importer must call handoff_done to flip RELEASED. if importer never calls, a background scanner reclaims after timeout.

anya: background scanner is necessary. add metrics for handoff_count, handoff_time_ms, handoff_reclaimed. also emit per-tenant labels.

jorge: memory visibility: when we flip to RELEASED we must publish metadata writes. use atomic_store_release on state and atomic_load_acquire when importer reads. otherwise we can have stale metadata observed and cause UAF.

maria: kernel API suggestion:
- ioctls or new dma-buf attrs: DMA_EXPORT_HANDOFF -> returns token
- allocator_handoff_complete(token) syscall
- admin reclaim: allocator_force_handoff(token) with reason code

sam: also add a fastpath for tiny hot allocations where we keep current refcounted behavior (HOT_FASTPATH). but then enable a validator thread that periodically scans exported fds and forces handoff if pins exceed threshold. hybrid mode reduces p99 impact for KV caches.

anya: I want debug assertions in dev builds: panic if exported fd closed while allocator reports HANDOFF_PENDING > 0 for that fd. to catch early. production would just log.

jorge: also add cookie versioning: token = crc32(allocator_gen || nonce || pid) signed with kernel secret. helps detect stale importer libs or ABI mismatches.

maria: test plan:
- unit: state transitions, token reuse/expiry, concurrent claim attempts
- stress: rapid export/import churn across tenants + zmq pause/resume to vary ordering
- fuzz: random reorderings of free/detach/close sequences
- integration: tenant shutdown leak test (no pinned pages after process death)

sam: corner case: process crash after import but before handoff_complete. background scanner should detect orphaned tokens and reclaim, but we also need netlink admin so control plane can force reclaim for customer incidents.

offload-bot: note scheduled job: orphan-handoff-scanner every 30m. metrics: orphan_handoffs_total, orphan_handoff_age_p95.

anya: edge perf: token handshake adds overhead per-export. mitigate by making token issuance lazy: only for allocators marked DMABUF_HANDOFF_REQUIRED or when exporter registers "will reuse" hint. most one-shot exports (send-to-renderer) can skip handshake.

jorge: for allocator internals, represent per-page state as atomic_u8 with bitflags: bit0 ACTIVE, bit1 HANDOFF_PENDING, bit2 RELEASED. atomic_cmpxchg transitions. Store token metadata in a side table keyed by page id to avoid enlarging hot page struct.

maria: logging format for reclaim events: {timestamp, token, age_ms, pid, tenant, allocator_gen, device}. include sample log line in RFC.

sam: who owns the RFC? I can prototype importer shim and a small userlib change to call the ioctl.

anya: i'll draft the RFC with state diagram and example ioctl proto. jorge, can you sketch the reclaim backoff and metrics buckets? maria, add token encoding and cookie verification notes.

jorge: will do, and i'll include a small fuzz runner harness that uses our existing tenant-stress infra.

maria: one more thought: fragmentation — when pages are stuck in HANDOFF_PENDING they fragment host staging pools. consider including a hint with token about residency intention (SHORT_LIVED vs LONG_LIVED) so allocator can bias fragmentation heuristics. e.g., SHORT_LIVED pages go to a fast reclaimable slab.

anya: nice. include that in token attrs. ok team, let's aim to have an RFC draft by Wed EOD. we'll iterate and land a prototype the sprint after. :thumbsup:

sam: cool. I'll run the shim through the stress harness and post results.

offload-bot: auto: created issue CI-1234 for orphaned-handoff-scanner followup.
